product.what: A web app for a job take-home: a customer-support AI agent for Paylane, a fictional fintech app (cards, transfers, refunds). The agent must follow a refund and verification policy even when customers push back, lie, or try to trick it.
screens: Playground: chat with the agent as one of 12 test customers. Next to the chat, every decision behind each reply is shown: which tools ran, whether each action was allowed or blocked and under which policy rule, and four probabilities from a classifier (fraud report, legal threat, account closure, attempt to change the rules).
Eval report: 12 scripted conversations, each run three times, with pass, fail or needs-review for every check, and the transcript behind each check.
audiences: Engineers at Fini who build AI support agents for a living. They are judging a job candidate, skim fast, and want to see why the agent did what it did.
Paylane's head of support, who is not technical and needs to understand at a glance what the agent does, what it refuses, and when it hands a customer to a person.
The candidate, demoing it live in a job interview over screen share.
product.success: Within one minute a reviewer understands the score and watches the agent refuse something, such as splitting a $180 refund into three $60 refunds, and can see exactly why.
product.must_avoid: Looking like a generic AI-generated dashboard or template.

built_ui.look: As built: a dark top bar with Playground and Eval report tabs. Playground: a left list of 13 synthetic test customers with a plain situation line each; a centre white sheet with numbered lines behind a thin gray margin rule, speaker labels in small capitals (CUSTOMER, AGENT), and between messages short notes with an icon and plain words, for example Checked identity: verified as Marcus Hill, Looked up txn_6001: $180.00, Hilton Hotels, settled, 5 days old, Handed to a person: ticket tk_0001 on a pale blue background, Refund not allowed: over the $75 limit (R4) in red on a pale red background; a composer under the sheet; a right Why panel showing the selected note’s tool, JSON input and result, the rule text, and four Jev readings as marks on a thin 0 to 1 line with a 0.5 tick and labels like Reports fraud 4% likely. One sans typeface (Public Sans) throughout. Eval report: a headline of conversations that passed every run, a table of conversations by run with Pass/Fail/Review pill badges with icons, and per-conversation views with run tabs, the numbered transcript and a list of checks with rule ids that highlight the lines they cite.
